description: The Harmonized World Soil Database version 2.0 is a global soil map at 30 arc-seconds (about 1 km) linked to a database of about 30,000 soil mapping units with their soil types and morphological, chemical and physical attributes. Compared with version 1.2 it describes seven depth layers from 0 to 200 cm instead of two, and adds attributes such as effective cation exchange capacity, total nitrogen, C/N ratio, aluminium saturation, USDA texture class and reference bulk density. It was produced by FAO and IIASA with ISRIC, the European Soil Bureau Network and the Chinese Academy of Sciences, and the revised v2.01 dates from September 2023. The raster, the Access database, a viewer program and the technical report are free downloads from the FAO soils portal, but the page read does not state a licence. Caveats: it harmonises national surveys of different ages and scales, so detail and reliability vary by country, and each mapping unit mixes several soils. For simulation it provides soil properties for crop and hydrological models, drought and flood exposure studies, and first estimates of ground conditions for pipelines, roads and foundations. It is related to the U.S. Drought Monitor and Census of Agriculture records in this catalogue, which add hazard and farm exposure data for the United States.
